articles.title: Investment Firm HarbourVest Partners Takes 20K SF at 9 West 57th Street
articles.narrative: HarbourVest Partners, a global private markets investment firm, has signed a 10-year lease for its inaugural New York City office. The firm will occupy nearly 20,000 square feet on the 49th floor of 9 West 57th Street, a prestigious Midtown office tower. The move reflects a strategic focus on attracting and retaining top talent by securing a high-caliber office space that aligns with the firm's business and provides an exceptional experience for clients and employees.

data_points.address: 9 West 57th Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: 49-story office building known for attracting prestigious financial and investment firms.

articles.market_intelligence: The average asking rent for office space in Midtown was $98.98 per square foot during the first half of 2026. A record asking rent at 9 West 57th Street was previously reported at $327.50 per square foot.

articles.title: Korean Grocery Sensation H Mart Wants to Conquer the Sun Belt
articles.narrative: H Mart, a Korean grocery chain, is aggressively expanding into Sun Belt markets including Florida, Texas, California, and Nevada, capitalizing on its growing popularity among both Asian American communities and a broader American audience. The company, which generates $2 billion in annual sales from over 100 locations, has distinguished itself by offering authentic imported Asian ingredients and a welcoming shopping experience. This expansion is driven by increasing immigration from East Asia and the rising purchasing power of Asian American households, particularly second-generation immigrants who are more affluent and seeking sophisticated products.

articles.title: Dedeaux Properties CEO Brett Dedeaux On California’s Next Industrial Cycle
articles.narrative: Dedeaux Properties CEO Brett Dedeaux discusses the recovery of the Southern California industrial market, noting a transition from a "reset" period to one of "recovery." Despite previous challenges like trade tariffs and interest rate hikes, Dedeaux observes "green shoots" of activity, with tenants resuming expansion plans and investors re-entering the market. He highlights the strong performance of advanced manufacturing and industrial outdoor storage (IOS) sectors, attributing Southern California's appeal to its skilled workforce and established vendor networks. The firm is also adapting its development strategies to address rising power demands in new facilities.

articles.title: Sunday Summary: Don’t Feel Embarrassed.
articles.narrative: This article is a weekly summary covering several key commercial real estate topics. It discusses the potential conflicts of interest arising from owners launching special servicing platforms, which allow them insight into competitors' distressed assets. The piece also explores the disconnect between strong REIT performance and their stock valuations, examines the near-collapse of the Pfizer headquarters conversion project due to concerns over third-party safety inspections, and highlights significant personnel changes within prominent CRE firms. Finally, it rounds up recent retail leasing activity in New York City and provides an update on retail investment trends in Southern California and South Florida.

articles.title: A bounce-back quarter for Minneapolis’ industrial sector
articles.narrative: The Minneapolis-St. Paul industrial market experienced a rebound in the second quarter, achieving nearly 488,000 square feet of positive net absorption, a significant improvement from the previous quarter's negative figures. This positive absorption occurred despite several large tenant move-outs, driven by strong demand for modern industrial facilities. While overall vacancy rates edged up slightly to 4.4% due to older building vacancies, and average asking rents softened to $9.12 per square foot, new construction activity accelerated with 3.4 million square feet under development, indicating continued investment in high-quality industrial space.
articles.market_intelligence: The Minneapolis-St. Paul industrial market saw a 20-basis-point increase in overall vacancy from the previous quarter and a 30-basis-point increase year-over-year. However, properties built in 2022 or later experienced a 20-basis-point decline in vacancy. Average asking rents declined 2% quarterly and 4.3% year-over-year, but remain 3.4% higher than three years ago. Leasing activity was down 24.4% from Q1 and 27.1% year-over-year, but the average lease size increased by nearly 17% quarterly and 20% year-over-year.

articles.title: Texas Icon Patti Miller: Turning business development into a strategic growth engine
articles.narrative: This article profiles Patti Miller, Vice President at E.E. Reed Construction, highlighting her 15-year career transforming business development into a strategic growth engine for the commercial construction firm. Miller's approach emphasizes disciplined strategy, accountability, and strong alignment between revenue generation, marketing, and operations. Her leadership has been instrumental in strengthening the firm's brand, deepening client relationships, and ensuring sustainable growth by intentionally pursuing projects that align with the company's values and operational readiness.

articles.title: Bonner Carrington, Sycamore Development announce opening of 168-unit multifamily development in North Dallas
articles.narrative: Bonner Carrington and Sycamore Development have opened Cypress Creek Montfort Drive, a 168-unit mixed-income multifamily community in North Dallas. The development provides much-needed affordable housing, with 116 units designated for residents earning 30% to 80% of the area median income and 52 market-rate units. The project aims to offer quality housing in a high-opportunity area, fostering a stronger workforce and supporting local businesses.

data_points.notable_features: Mixed-income community with 116 income-restricted units and 52 market-rate units; features a four-story building with structured parking, resort-style pool, fitness center, business center, and pet spa.
data_points.project_notes: Financing included Federal 9% Low-Income Housing Tax Credit equity, construction and permanent financing, a soft loan from the City of Dallas, and funding from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) Program. 41 units are supported by the Walker Settlement Voucher program.

articles.title: KAI, SmithGroup help deliver long-awaited aquatics center to DeSoto
articles.narrative: The City of DeSoto officially opened its new $53 million Aquatics & Recreation Center (ARC) in April, a project that has been envisioned by residents for over a decade. Designed in partnership by KAI and SmithGroup, the 75,000-square-foot, two-story facility aims to serve both community recreation needs and provide a competitive venue for various sports. The center is part of a larger master plan for Curtistene S. McCowan Park, which includes future amenities like an amphitheater and walking trails.

data_points.notable_features: Features an 8-lane competition pool, leisure pool with observation decks, a 400-foot suspended fitness track, fitness and strength training areas, meeting rooms, locker rooms, gymnasiums, administrative offices, and social gathering spaces.
data_points.project_notes: The project is part of a larger master plan for Curtistene S. McCowan Park, which includes future plans for an amphitheater, water features, sculpture garden, walking trails, and additional sports fields.

articles.title: Summer camp sales mark the next chapter in Simad’s collapse
articles.narrative: The Shabsels brothers' summer camp empire, Simad, is being dismantled through bankruptcy proceedings, with two camps finding buyers. Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav made a $68 million stalking horse bid for Mohawk Day Camp in Westchester, while Camp Achim in the Catskills sold for $7 million to its long-term operator. These sales are part of the ongoing liquidation of a portfolio that was once valued at $466 million but became extraordinarily leveraged through Israeli bond market financing and high-cost merchant cash advance loans, leading to a liquidity crisis and default.

data_points.notable_features: Mohawk Day Camp is located in Westchester, NY; Camp Achim is located in the Catskills, NY.
data_points.project_notes: The sales are part of the bankruptcy proceedings for Simad, the Shabsels brothers' summer camp empire. Mohawk Day Camp's sale was initiated with a stalking horse bid.

articles.title: Summer spotlight: Lake Tahoe, where Big Tech summers (and skis)
articles.market: Lake Tahoe, NV / Lake Tahoe, CA
articles.narrative: Lake Tahoe's luxury real estate market, particularly on the Nevada side, is experiencing a boom driven by Bay Area tech billionaires seeking tax advantages and a high-end lifestyle. Recent record-breaking sales include a $125 million off-market purchase by a SpaceX board member and a $42 million acquisition by a Google co-founder. While the ultra-luxury segment thrives, the market for homes under $20 million has softened, with sellers adjusting prices to current conditions. The influx of wealth has also attracted significant real estate development, with major projects underway or planned, including the redevelopment of the Hyatt Regency Lake Tahoe Resort and the Cal Neva Resort, despite some community opposition to privatization efforts.

articles.market_intelligence: The Nevada side of Lake Tahoe is approximately 40 percent more expensive than the California side, primarily due to tax benefits. Pricing for homes below the $20 million mark has softened compared to 2021 levels.

articles.title: South Florida Dirt: The soccer stars who planted a flag in South Florida
articles.narrative: This article provides a roundup of significant residential real estate transactions involving prominent soccer players in South Florida, highlighting their long-term investment in the region. The transactions include waterfront mansions, luxury condos, and residential plots, reflecting the area's appeal to high-net-worth individuals. The market has seen substantial activity, with several multi-million dollar deals closing in recent years, often involving properties with extensive amenities and prime waterfront locations.
articles.market_intelligence: West Palm Beach and Miami exhibit the widest and second-widest gaps, respectively, in the U.S. between luxury and non-luxury home and condo prices.

articles.title: Evanston greenlights apartment complex despite historic Black church’s objections
articles.narrative: The Evanston City Council has approved zoning for a five-story, 30-unit apartment complex at 1103 and 1105 Emerson Street, despite objections from the adjacent Ebenezer AME Church. The church raised concerns about the development's height, density, potential impact on its structural integrity, and noise from future tenants. As a result, the developer, PM Properties, agreed to a "good neighbor" ordinance, which includes specific requirements for building materials, noise monitoring, and a taller fence for the church's parking lot.

data_points.notable_features: Three units are designated as affordable housing for residents earning 40% of the area's median income.
data_points.project_notes: The development includes a 'good neighbor' ordinance requiring PM Properties to obtain city approval for exterior materials, replace building elevations, submit documents on the church's condition, avoid rooftop sound systems, build a taller fence for the church, and implement onsite noise monitoring.

articles.title: SF’s housing frenzy migrates to Marin, Ian Jacobs doubles down downtown, Transamerica gets moving
articles.narrative: The San Francisco housing market's intense competition, marked by homes selling significantly above asking price, is driving a spillover effect into Marin County, which is now experiencing double-digit median price jumps. This trend, fueled by the artificial intelligence boom centered in San Francisco, is a departure from previous tech cycles where Marin's lack of public rail made it less attractive to homebuyers. Meanwhile, in downtown San Francisco, Ian Jacobs, a scion of the Reichmann real estate dynasty, has acquired the four-story retail and office building at 180 Post Street for $48.5 million, continuing his strategy of assembling commercial properties in the Union Square district. Separately, Yoda PLC, the new owner of the Transamerica Pyramid, has signed seven new office leases totaling 113,000 square feet and announced plans for significant renovations to Two Transamerica, an adjacent building, with new amenities expected to be completed by Q4 this year.

data_points.notable_features: Anchored by a long-term lease with a luxury jeweler.
data_points.project_notes: Part of Project Uris, a $75 million plan to acquire 3 million square feet of San Francisco commercial buildings.

articles.market_intelligence: San Francisco's housing market has seen a 1,700 percent increase in homes sold for at least $1 million over asking price this year. Marin County was the only Bay Area housing market as of July to experience a double-digit median price jump over last year.

articles.title: Brookfield, CPP Taking LXP Industrial Private in $5.2B Deal
articles.narrative: Brookfield Asset Management and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board have agreed to acquire LXP Industrial Trust in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $5.2 billion, including net debt and preferred equity. LXP Industrial Trust owns a significant portfolio of 108 warehouse and logistics facilities, totaling approximately 53 million square feet, primarily located in the Sunbelt and Midwest regions of the U.S. This acquisition represents the culmination of LXP's strategic repositioning to become a pure-play industrial REIT with a high-quality portfolio and development program, aligning with Brookfield's strategy of investing in real estate with durable cash flows and value creation opportunities.

data_points.notable_features: Portfolio comprises 108 properties in the Sunbelt and Midwest regions.
data_points.project_notes: The transaction includes a 40-day 'go-shop' period expiring August 28.
